questions.question: Does `MarmotGroupEvents` in `src/client/group/marmot-group.ts` include `rollback: (info: RollbackInfo) => void` as a typed entry alongside existing events? Does `group.on('rollback', handler)` compile without TypeScript error? Show (a) the updated `MarmotGroupEvents` type, (b) a `tsc --noEmit` invocation or `pnpm build` output confirming zero errors.

After a rollback, does `ingest()` yield invalidation records for application messages that were decrypted under the losing epoch, and does each record carry the event id of the message? Does an integration test in `src/__tests__/integration/ingest-commit-race.test.ts` assert that the event ids in `RollbackInfo.invalidatedMessages` exactly match the set of messages that were decrypted prior to rollback? Show the test's assertion block.

After a rollback restores the epoch-N snapshot and re-applies the winner, are events previously in the "unreadable" set that were encrypted under the winner's epoch keys re-attempted, and do they succeed — appearing in the final `ingest()` result as successfully decrypted rather than unreadable? Show the integration test assertion that confirms previously-unreadable events are now in the decrypted set.

When a rollback occurs, does `MarmotGroup` emit exactly one `rollback` event with a `RollbackInfo` payload where `targetEpoch` equals the epoch of the snapshot restored (the epoch before the losing commit was applied) and `newHeadCommitEventId` equals the winning commit's Nostr event id? Does the integration test register a spy on `group.on('rollback', ...)` and assert exactly one emission with these values? Show the spy setup and assertion.

When only one commit exists for an epoch (no race condition), does `ingest()` emit zero `rollback` events? Does a test verify the spy count is zero after normal single-committer ingest? Show the no-event assertion.

Does the per-ingest message-tracking bookkeeping (the structure that records which messages were decrypted under the in-progress epoch) leave no state leak between `ingest()` calls — i.e. is the per-call record cleared at the start or end of each invocation, so a subsequent non-rollback ingest does not inherit the prior call's epoch-message list? Confirm by reading the `ingest()` code around the bookkeeping initialization.

Does S3's implementation of message tracking and event emission remain confined to `src/client/group/marmot-group.ts` with no changes to `src/core/group-message.ts`, `epoch-snapshot.ts`, or any file in `src/extra/`? List every file modified by S3 and confirm each is within the S3 scope boundary from `stories.json`.

Could the rollback event emission and invalidation bookkeeping in `marmot-group.ts` be deleted and rewritten without modifying any file outside `marmot-group.ts` and the integration test file? If not, which dependencies exist, and do they flow through the `RollbackInfo` seam contract declared in `stories.json`?

Is the rollback event emission tested with a real EventEmitter-style `group.on('rollback', spy)` call (not just checking the return value of `ingest()`), so the test confirms both that the event fires and that its payload has the correct shape? Does the test also confirm that `group.on('rollback', ...)` compiles — i.e. TypeScript accepts the string literal `'rollback'` as a valid event name for this group instance?

Does the library's `rollback` event emission follow the existing event-emission pattern for other `MarmotGroupEvents` entries (same emitter call style, same error-handling discipline) so consumers can subscribe without observing any behavioral difference from other event types? Confirm by comparing the rollback emission code with an existing event emission in `marmot-group.ts`.

The `#messagesByEpoch` map is a permanent instance field (not cleared per `ingest()` call). Does it grow unboundedly if the caller issues many non-rollback ingest calls with application messages across many epochs? The rollback cleanup path deletes epochs strictly above `targetEpoch`, but epochs below or equal to `targetEpoch` are never pruned. Is this bounded by the number of epochs the local member has been in the group, and is that acceptable for the expected group lifetime?

The test for AC-EVT-1 / AC-MSG-1 wraps the winner's MLS bytes with the LOSER's epoch-2 exporter secret so the member (at epoch 2) can NIP-44-decrypt the outer envelope. Is this a valid simulation of the production MIP-03 rollback path, or does the real S4 past-epoch decryption window behave differently in a way that would cause the rollback path to never fire in production with winner-epoch-1 commits delivered after the member has advanced to epoch 2?
